rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib glosses adbara as turning away and presenting one's back.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : أدبر أي اعرض وولى دبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's striving against the sign came from defiance and obstinacy, not belief that it could truly be matched.
rows.anchor: يجتهد في معارضة الآية تمردا وعنادا لا اعتقادا بأنها يمكن معارضتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His effort was a false pretext to evade the gathering or court.
rows.anchor: فهو تعلل بالباطل دفعا للمجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, “striving” is a circumstantial qualifier of the subject of “turned away,” meaning he hurried and exerted himself.
rows.anchor: وهو حال من فاعل أدبر بمعنى مسرعا مجتهدا

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf pictures Pharaoh fleeing in terror and running quickly when he saw the serpent.
rows.anchor: وفي "الكشاف" لما رأى الثعبان أدبر مرعوبا يسرع في مشيته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes Pharaoh as a rash, impulsive man.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله كان رجلا طياشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads “he gathered” as Pharaoh assembling the sorcerers and their devices, linking this to another account of Pharaoh gathering his plot.
rows.anchor: {فحشر} أي فجمع السحرة لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh may have summoned all the people and made the announcement himself at the gathering or through a herald.
rows.anchor: فنادى} بنفسه في المقام الذي اجتمعوا فيه ، معه أو بواسطة المنادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His declaration means that he claimed there was no lord above him.
rows.anchor: {فقال} لقيامة مقام الحكومة والسلطنة {أنا ربكم الاعلى} لا رب فوقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superlative can refer to his rank over the kings and officials under his rule.
rows.anchor: على أن تكون صيغة التفضيل بالنسبة إلى من كان تحت ولايته من الملوك والأمراء

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kāshifī interprets Pharaoh as saying that the idols resembling him were all gods and that he was higher than them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) : يعني أصنام كه بر صورت منند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the sorcerers were defeated, Moses was told that he was the higher one, since victory over the magic was victory over Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قيل لموسى عليه السلام في مقابلة هذا الكلام إنك أنت الأعلى لأن الغلبة على سحره غلبة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was not claiming to have created the heavens, earth, mountains, plants, or animals; that claim would be self-evidently false.
rows.anchor: لم يرد بهذا القول إنه خالق السموات والأرض والجبال والنبات والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who doubts that created things have a creator is insane; an insane person could not have been sent a messenger by God.
rows.anchor: ومن شك فيه كان مجنونا ولو كان مجنونا لما جاز من الله بعثة الرسول إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather, Pharaoh was a materialist who denied the Creator and resurrection, claiming that he alone nurtured and benefited his people.
rows.anchor: بل الرجل كان دهريا منكرا للصانع والحشر والنشر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says that after his humiliation and helplessness before the transformed staff, Pharaoh should not have made the claim; he seemed delirious and unaware of his words.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : كان ينبغي له عند ظهور ذله وعجزه بانقلاب العصا حية إن لا يقول ذلك القول

rows.speaker: الإمام القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī relates that Iblīs could not bear Pharaoh's boast: Iblīs had claimed good for himself and suffered calamity, so he wondered what would befall Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: (إمام قشيري رحمه الله) : در لطائف آورده كه إبليس اين سخن شنيده كفت مراطاقت اين سخن نيست

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha asks the Prophet how people, and then women, will be gathered; he answers that they will be barefoot and naked.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر إن عائشة رضي الله عنهما ، قالت يا رسول الله كيف يحشر الناس قال حفاة عراة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: After ʿĀʾisha exclaims at women being among men in that state, the Prophet recites this verse.
rows.anchor: فقرأ رسول الله عليه السلام هذه الآية لكل امرىء الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People flee because relatives may demand restitution for wrongs: misused wealth, neglected parents, unlawful food given to a wife, or failure to teach and guide children.
rows.anchor: وأما الفرار حذرا من مطالبتهم بالتبعات بأن يقول الإنسان واسيتني بمالك والأبوان قصرت في برنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Cain flees Abel and prophets flee close relatives; Bursevī says these cases are not the flight meant here.
rows.anchor: كما يروى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إن يفر قابيل منأخيه هابيل ويفر النبي من أمه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that a person flees companions and relatives so they will not see his shameful condition.
rows.anchor: ما يروى إن الرجل بفر من أصحابه وأقربائه لئلا يروه على ما هو عليه من سوء الحال

rows.speaker: بعض المشايخ
rows.claim: A shaykhly saying contrasts being occupied with oneself today, which leaves one occupied with oneself tomorrow, with being occupied with God.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المشايخ من كان اليوم مشغولا بنفسه فهو غدا مشغول بنفسه

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh says that self-occupation distracts from God through worldly desires or, in the afterlife, through the preoccupation described in this verse; he asks when one will devote oneself to knowing and obeying God.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ إذا شغلتك نفسك في دنياك وعقباك عن ربك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A gnostic remains among people outwardly while separating from them inwardly.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : العارف مع الخلق ولكنه يفارقهم بقلبه

rows.speaker: الشعر
rows.claim: The cited poem portrays the beloved as the heart's interlocutor while the body remains open to whoever wishes to sit nearby.
rows.anchor: ولقد جعلتك في الفؤاد محدثي وابحت جسمي من أراد جلوسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bright faces describe the final division of the people just mentioned into the blessed and the wretched after their great ordeal.
rows.anchor: بيان لمآل أمر المذكورين وأنقسامهم إلى السعداء والأشقياء بعد ذكر وقوعهم في داهية دهياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Faces” is the subject and “radiant” its predicate; “that day” refers to the day when a person flees and modifies the predicate.
rows.anchor: فوجوه مبتدأ أو إن كانت نكرة لكونها في حيز التنوين ومسفرة خبره ويومئذ أي يوم إذ يفر لمرء متعلق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces are bright and gleaming through the luminosity of their selves and qualities; the word evokes dawn becoming light.
rows.anchor: أي مضيئة متهللة بنورية ذواتهم وصفاتها من أسفر الصبح إذا أضاء

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt notes that isfār is specifically associated with color.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات : الأسفار يختص باللون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the radiance as a result of night prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إن ذلك من قيام الليل

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says that abundant night prayer makes one's face beautiful by day.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "من كثرت صلاته بالليل حسن وجهه بالنهار"

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the radiance as traces of ablution.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك من آثار الوضوء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view attributes the radiance to the dust accumulated through striving in God's path.
rows.anchor: وقيلم ن طول ما أغبرت في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed faces laugh and rejoice at the lasting bliss and enduring joy they witness.
rows.anchor: {ضاحكة مستبشرة} بما تشاهد من النعيم المقيم والهبجة الدائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī identifies the surah as Meccan and reports a count of twenty-nine or twenty-eight verses.
rows.anchor: تسع أو ثمان وعشرون آية مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred parsing, “the sun” is nominative as the subject of an omitted verb explained by the following verb, since a subject cannot precede its verb.
rows.anchor: ارتفاع الشمس على إنه فاعل لفعل مضمر يفسره المذكور

rows.speaker: بعض
rows.claim: Some grammarians instead parse “the sun” as a subject because supplying an omitted element departs from the default.
rows.anchor: وعند البعض على الابتداء لأن التقدير خلاف الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the first parsing because idhā has conditional force and a condition is associated with a verb; on either parsing, the clause is genitive as the complement of idhā.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى لأن إذا فيها معنى الشرط والشرط مختص بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takwir literally means wrapping, like wrapping a turban by folding its parts around one another.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كورت لفت من كورت العمامة إذا لففتها بضم بعض أجزائها لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is the sun's removal from its station: as folded clothing is lifted away, its coiling figuratively denotes its removal.
rows.anchor: فكان بين السماء والرفع علاقة اللزوم فتكويرها كناية عن رفعها

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī allows literal coiling: even if the sun is a solid sphere, God can make it capable of being spread out and then coiled.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي ولام نع من إرادة المعنى الحقيقي أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the sun's dispersed light is rolled up; the attribution is figurative or assumes an omitted noun, and the rolling signifies extinguishing its light.
rows.anchor: وأما لف ضوئها المنبسط في الآفاق المنتشر في الأقطار بأن يكون إسناد كورت إلى ضمير الشمس مجازيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this light interpretation, literal rolling is impossible because light is an accident and cannot itself be wrapped.
rows.anchor: إذ لا مساغ لإرادة المعنى الحقيقي لأن الضوء لكونه من الأعراض لا يتصور فيه اللف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some object that al-Kashshāf errs in saying the light cannot be rolled while the sun remains, since God can blot out its light and leave it in place.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن الله قادر على أن يطمس نورها مع بقائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī answers that removing a necessary concomitant entails removing what it necessarily accompanies.
rows.anchor: وجوابه ما أشير إليه من حكم الاستلزام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that the sun is cast from its orbit onto the earth, using takwīr for throwing something onto the ground.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى كورت ألقيت من فلكها على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says the sun and moon will be two lights coiled and cast into the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : إن الشمس والقمر نوران مكوران في النار يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: When told the hadith, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī asks what fault the sun and moon have.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر هذا الحديث عند الحسن البصري رحمه الله ، قال : وما ذنبهما

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam rejects al-Ḥasan's objection because the sun and moon are inanimate and cannot be harmed by the Fire; their presence may instead increase its heat.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام سؤال الحسن ساقط لأن الشمس والقمر جمادان

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī says they are placed in Hell to torment its worshippers, especially worshippers of the heavenly bodies, not to punish the inanimate bodies themselves.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال الطيبي تكويرهما فيها ليعذب بهما أهل النار لا سيما عباد الأنوار

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: The sun and moon are unaccountable beings in Hell, comparable in their status there to Hellfire itself and its appointed angels.
rows.anchor: فإنها بمعزل عن التكليف بل سبيلهما في النار سبيل النار نفسها وسبيل الملائكة الموكلين بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-birr, with fatḥa, means truthfulness, obedience, and beneficence.
rows.anchor: جمع بر بالفتح وهوبمعنى الصادق والمطيع والمحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among good deeds, the greatest is affirming God's oneness, followed by kindness to parents, students' kindness to teachers, and seekers' kindness to their shaykhs.
rows.anchor: وأحسن الحسنات لا إله إلا الله ثم بر الوالدين وبر التلامذة للأساتذة

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān defines the righteous person as one whose beneficence is broadly extended, who obeys God, and who does as much good for people as possible.
rows.anchor: كما قال في فتح الرحمن هو الذي قد أطرد بره عموما فبرر به في طاعته إياه

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith urges children to treat their parents as kindly as parents treated their children.
rows.anchor: (وفي الحديث) : بروا آباءهم كما بروا أبناءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bliss is the bliss of Paradise and its reward; the tanwīn magnifies it.
rows.anchor: {لفى نعيم} وهو نعيم الجنة وثوابها والتنوين للتخفيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fujjār is the plural of fājir, and fujūr means tearing the veil of religious integrity.
rows.anchor: جمع فاجر والفجور شق ستر الديانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text's Persian gloss describes the wicked as liars and deniers of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وبدرستى كه دروغ كويان ومنكران حشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire means Hell and its punishment, while the tanwīn conveys intimidation.
rows.anchor: {لفى جحيم} أي النار وعذابها والتنوين للتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses explain the end for which deeds are recorded: either bliss or Hell.
rows.anchor: والجملتان بيان لما يكتبون لأجله وهو أن الغاية إما النعيم وإما الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritually, bliss signifies remembrance, obedience, gnosis, witnessing, presence, and union; Hell signifies heedlessness, sin, ignorance, veiling, absence, and separation.
rows.anchor: الذكر والطاعة والمعرفة والشهود والحضور والوصال وإلى جحيم الغفلة والمعصية والجهل

rows.speaker: الخواص
rows.claim: Al-Khawwāṣ says bliss is delightful when it comes from God, and Hell is delightful when it comes through Him.
rows.anchor: قال الخواص رحمه الله ، طاب النعيم إذا كان منه وطاب الجحيم إذا كان به

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The cited Mathnawī verses portray the sovereign's presence as making even a wilderness paradise, illustrating the spiritual meaning of bliss.
rows.anchor:
وفي المثنوى :
هر كجا باشد شه مارا بساط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They enter it” either describes Hell or begins a new sentence answering how the damned fare: they undergo its heat.
rows.anchor: {يصلونها} أما صفة لجحيم أو استئناف مبني على سؤال نشأ عن تهويلها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says the unbeliever enters the Fire, suffers its heat, and encounters it bodily.
rows.anchor: كما قال الخليل صلى الكافر النار قاسي حرها وباشره ببدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage does not give a matching description of Paradise because its immediate subject is sinful deniers and a warning; mentioning the righteous clarifies their opposite.
rows.anchor: ولم يصف النعيم بما يلائمه لأن ما سبق من الكلام كان في المكذبين الفجرة لأن المقام مقام التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment is the day of recompense that the deniers used to reject.
rows.anchor: يوم الدين} يوم الجزاء الذي كانوا يكذبون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned will not be absent from Hell for even an instant; the point is their lasting presence, not a temporary absence.
rows.anchor: طرفه عين يعني دروجاويد باشند وبيرون نيايند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were not wholly absent from Hell even earlier, since they experienced its heat in their graves, as the Prophet's report likens the grave to a garden or a pit of fire.
rows.anchor: بل كانوا يجدون سمومها في قبورهم حسبما قال النبي عليه السلام ، القبر روضة من رياض الجنة أو حفرة من حفر النيران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in “what has made you know” applies to anyone capable of knowing; “what” is the subject, “made you know” its predicate, and the following “what” describes the Day.
rows.anchor: الخطاب لكل من يأتى منه الدراية وما مبتدأ وإدراك خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative seeks a description, whereas the other term seeks the reality or explanation of a name; the Day's reality exceeds what creatures can conceive.
rows.anchor: وما لطلب الوصف وإنك ان وضعه لطلب الحقيقة وشرح الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording says that no one had yet conveyed the Day's true scope to the addressee; its horror exceeds the range of created understanding.
rows.anchor: أي شيء عجيب هو في الهول والفظاعة أي ما أدراك إلى هذا الآن أحد كنه أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition with thumma intensifies the rank of the warning, reinforces it, and magnifies the terror of the Day; repeating its name rather than using a pronoun heightens its gravity.
rows.anchor: تكرير بثم امفيدة للترقي في الرتبة للتأكيد وزيادة التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “a day when no soul controls anything for another” briefly explains the Day after its reality has been left obscure.
rows.anchor: بيان إجمال لشأن يوم الدين أثر إبهامه وبيان خروجه عن دائرة علوم الخلق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every Qur'anic “what has made you know” is answered by God, whereas “what makes you know” is left undisclosed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كل ما في القرآن من قوله تعالى : [الانفطار : 17-19]{ومآ أدرااك} فقد أدراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Day” may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject (“it is a day”), or accusative under an implied “remember.”
rows.anchor: ويوم مرفوع على إنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day's “soul” includes angels, humans, and jinn, and “anything” includes whatever could bring benefit or avert harm.
rows.anchor: ودخل في نفس كل نفس ملكية وبشرية وجنية وفي شيء كل ما كن من قبيل جلب المنفعة أو دفع المضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase says that on that day the whole affair belongs to God alone, when no soul can control anything for another.
rows.anchor: والأمر} كله {يومااذ} أي يوم إذ لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command, judgment, and decree belong to the obeyed Sovereign, while all creatures are subdued beneath divine dominion.
rows.anchor: فإن الأمر والحكم والقضاء من شأن الملك المطاع والخلق كلهم مقهورون تحت سطوات الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-amr means one of the affairs: every matter of the gathered people is in God's hand, with no one else able to dispose of it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون واحد الأمور فإن أمور أهل المحشر كلها بيده تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns of human weakness: wealth, children, helpers, and intercessors will not help as they do in worldly life; faith, righteousness, and obedience will.
rows.anchor: أخبر تعالى بضعف الناس يومئذ وإنه لا ينفعهم الأموال والأولاد والأعوان والشفعاء كما في الدنيا بل ينفعهم الإيمان والبر والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one will speak except by God's permission and command.
rows.anchor: وإنه لا يقدر أحد أن يتكلم إلا بإذن الله وأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's authority is real in both worlds, though the veiled person imagines that God allotted him some worldly control; the Hereafter reveals that God has no rival or partner, even in appearance.
rows.anchor: لأمر له في الدنيا والآخرة في الحقيقة وإن كان يظهر سلطانه في الآخرة بالنسبة إلى المحجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a threat to claimants and those who oppose God, and a warning of His force and might.
rows.anchor: وفيه تهديد لأرباب الدعاوي وأصحاب المخالفة وتنبيه على عظيم بطشه تعالى

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith promises that reciting Sūrat al-Infiṭār earns a good deed for every grave and every drop of water, and that God will set the reciter's affairs right on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث من قرأ إذا السماء انفطرت أعطاه الله من الأجر بعدد كل قبر حسنة
